title: Redwood discovery - Stellar Payments latency & throughput
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency requirements, streaming support and token/sec benchmarking across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment options; discussed security (SOC2, SAML, KMS) and next steps for benchmarks and pricing.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Stellar), Priya Shah (SRE Lead), Ethan Miller (ML Eng)
Links shared: security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack), benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://docs.example.com/steller-benchmarks)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Diego our systems engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Liam O'Connor: Good, thanks. Quick heads up, we're on a tight timeline for Q2 pilot, so want to understand whether hosted meets our p95 and concurrency needs or we should plan Dedicated or Private.
[00:18] Diego Ruiz: totally. quick agenda — gather your p95 targets, concurrency, streaming needs, and token/sec expectations; then we'll map to hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs and next steps for a benchmark run.
[00:28] Priya Shah: Great. to frame it: our payment flows need sub-300ms p95 for short prompts (<64 tokens) for fraud scoring path, and ~1s p95 for longer conversational flows (~256 tokens) at 10 concurrent transactions peak. streaming is required for a subset of customers for real-time approvals.
[00:45] Ethan Miller: just to add, in ML infra we batch requests internally but we can't have large tail latencies — p95 is our SLA, p99 is less critical but still visible. Also we like to measure tokens/sec for throughput planning: expect bursts up to 2000 tokens/sec across the cluster.
[01:05] Diego Ruiz: ok that's helpful. when you say 10 concurrent, is that 10 long-running streaming connections or 10 parallel short requests?
[01:12] Priya Shah: mix — about 6 streaming sessions and 4 short scoring calls concurrent at peak.
[01:20] Maya Patel: perfect. on security side, are there compliance constraints beyond SOC2? do you need SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs, KMS/HSM integration?
[01:28] Liam O'Connor: SOC2 is must, and yes SAML SSO with Okta. for Private we may need a customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; for Hosted we need assurances around audit logs and encryption at rest.
[01:40] Diego Ruiz: Redwood Hosted is SOC2, supports SAML SSO and offers audit logs; for customer-managed KMS and VPC you would be looking at Private. Dedicated is a middle ground — reserved capacity with stronger isolation but KMS options vary by contract. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[01:58] Priya Shah: cool. on latency budgets — you've mentioned continuous batching and KV cache in your docs. how much does KV cache help for prefix-heavy traffic? our scoring calls include long customer context sometimes.
[02:12] Diego Ruiz: KV cache can dramatically reduce token generation for repeated prefixes. if your workload reuses prompts we often see 40-70% token cost reduction and lower p95. for short scoring (<64 tokens) caching impact is smaller but still helpful for alignment tokens.
[02:30] Ethan Miller: benchmark question — we want token/sec numbers for our exact model (we run a 13B open model quantized to int8). can you run benchmarks on a quantized 13B with 256-context and streaming enabled?
[02:42] Maya Patel: yes we can. typical hosted catalog includes several optimized variants; for dedicated we can run your quantized model on assigned GPU fleets. we'll need a sample model artifact and representative prompts.
[02:55] Liam O'Connor: timeline wise, can you do a run next week? we want results within 7 days to decide on procurement.
[03:01] Diego Ruiz: likely yes — we'll propose a benchmark plan after this call. note: for streaming p95 is influenced more by network hops and region. which region are you in?
[03:10] Priya Shah: primary traffic is eu-west-1 with failover to us-east-1.
[03:15] Diego Ruiz: got it. Hosted can route eu-west-1 with local edge and we can measure for p95 there; Dedicated or Private in your VPC will likely shave off 20-40ms due to fewer hops.
[03:28] Maya Patel: cost tradeoffs — for high concurrency and sustained throughput Dedicated often reduces unit cost, but Hosted is faster to set up and we can do a short pilot. Private is highest up-front.
[03:38] Liam O'Connor: what about autoscaling? bursts may jump above 10 concurrency to ~50 for short windows (couple minutes).
[03:45] Diego Ruiz: Redwood's autoscaler supports burst capacity; on Hosted we have soft limits and can increase with prior notice. Dedicated gives you headroom; Private you'd manage autoscaling with our control plane. for very spiky workloads we recommend a hybrid: Hosted as primary with Dedicated reserved for peak.
[04:02] Priya Shah: ok good. let's dig into p95 numbers: for our 13B int8 at 256 tokens, what's typical p95 on a T4 vs A10G vs H100?
[04:12] Diego Ruiz: rough numbers, ballpark: T4s see higher latency — p95 for 256-token generation might be in the 800ms-1.5s range depending on batching; A10G/A30 gives better throughput around 400-700ms; H100 with optimized kernels and fused attention can get sub-300ms p95 for 256 tokens in low-concurrency setups. those are approximate; we'll run exacts with your model.
[04:36] Ethan Miller: and for streaming, is there a difference in p95 per token vs p95 for first-byte? we care about time-to-first-token for UX.
[04:44] Diego Ruiz: good point — streaming first-byte latency often dominates perceived latency. our runtime optimizes for time-to-first-token via small initial batch and low-latency routing. p95 for first-byte is usually 100-200ms lower than full-generation p95 for short prompts.
[04:59] Maya Patel: also important: p95 definition — do you want end-to-end including network from your client to our edge, or server-side only?
[05:05] Priya Shah: end-to-end please, include client to edge, that aligns with our SLA.
[05:10] Maya Patel: noted. we'll include network hops and region measurements in the benchmark.
[05:15] Liam O'Connor: what about tokenization differences — we've seen different token/sec depending on tokenizer implementation. can that affect results?
[05:22] Diego Ruiz: yes, tokenizer and IO overhead can change tokens/sec by 5-15%. for true apples-to-apples we request you send the tokenized prompt set or run the tokenizer in our harness.
[05:33] Ethan Miller: we'll provide the tokenized prompt set.
[05:36] Priya Shah: security again — for Hosted, do you provide customer-specific audit logs export or only in-console?
[05:42] Maya Patel: Hosted provides audit logs export via S3 and can be forwarded to your SIEM. we'll include the exact retention options in the security pack.
[05:50] Liam O'Connor: ok thanks. can you walk through a sample benchmark plan?
[05:54] Diego Ruiz: sure — Plan: 1) collect sample artifacts (model weights or container + tokenized prompts), 2) define scenarios (short scoring 64 tokens, long conv 256 tokens, streaming sessions), 3) run three runs per region (eu-west-1, us-east-1) under three concurrency profiles (10 steady, 50 spike, 200 stress), 4) measure p95, p99, tokens/sec, time-to-first-token, and cost-per-1M tokens. We'll also include KV cache on/off and batching profiles.
[06:28] Maya Patel: we'll also run a Dedicated run on a reserved node group to compare unit economics and latencies.
[06:33] Priya Shah: do you simulate network egress or do we need to set up a client runner from our network?
[06:38] Diego Ruiz: we can run an end-to-end agent from a colocated VM in your VPC for Private or Dedicated; for Hosted we'll run from our edge in eu-west-1 but we can also accept a client runner from your side if you want exact client-to-edge metrics.
[06:51] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. pricing ask: can you send both hosted per-token and dedicated reserved pricing scenarios?
[06:57] Maya Patel: yes, we'll send pricing tiers: hosted per-token with volume discounts, and dedicated reserved cost models (monthly commit + overage).
[07:05] Ethan Miller: any limitations on streaming protocols? we use websockets with chunked token delivery.
[07:11] Diego Ruiz: websockets are supported, and we have examples of chunked streaming. we'll share the SDK snippet. caveat: on low-latency streaming at very high concurrency you might see more socket churn — we recommend connection pooling for large fleets.
[07:27] Priya Shah: ok, on fallback behavior — if you lose dedicated capacity do you auto-failover to hosted? we need seamless failover for availability.
[07:34] Maya Patel: yes, Redwood supports policy-driven routing and automated fallback to compatible model variants in Hosted if Dedicated capacity is constrained; we'll document the failover SLAs.
[07:44] Liam O'Connor: great. any notes about quantization differences — int8 vs int4 — how reliable are int4 perf gains?
[07:50] Diego Ruiz: int4 can improve throughput and lower memory but may have quality regressions depending on model; we recommend evaluation sets. Redwood Optimize has quantization profiles and suggestions; we'll run both int8 and int4 in benchmarks if you want.
[08:03] Maya Patel: ok recap time — i'll summarize what we discussed and next steps.
[08:08] Diego Ruiz: quick question — for the p95 target sub-300ms for 64 token path, that's pretty aggressive. is that end-to-end or server-only?
[08:15] Priya Shah: end-to-end, includes our client. we know it's tight but that's our user experience target.
[08:21] Diego Ruiz: two possible approaches: 1) keep prompts very short + aggressive KV cache in Dedicated or Private with region-local deployment; 2) optimize model variant (smaller model for scoring) and use H100s or similar. We'll include recommendations.
[08:37] Maya Patel: action items and timeline — Diego will run a technical benchmark plan and propose VM/region matrix; I'll send pricing and security pack; Stellar team to provide tokenized prompts and model artifacts. target to deliver benchmark results within 7 business days.
[08:52] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. last question: who will be our Redwood point-of-contact for engineering during the run?
[08:57] Maya Patel: Diego will be primary SE contact; cc me for contracts/pricing.
[09:02] Priya Shah: ok thanks folks.
[09:05] Maya Patel: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with a benchmark plan doc and calendar invite for end-to-end test.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'K V cache', 'H100' occasionally as 'H one zero zero'), filler words and overlaps, speaker labels are mostly accurate.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim in meeting):
- Redwood to run benchmarks (Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private) using Stellar's 13B int8 model and tokenized prompts; measure p95/p99, tokens/sec, time-to-first-token, and cost models.
- Redwood to send security pack and detailed pricing spreadsheet.
- Stellar to provide tokenized prompts, model artifact (or access), and confirm eu-west-1 test runner details.

End of transcript.
